nodes.title: BASE PROMPT
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> 是 <Picture 1> 中的年轻女子，黑色长发，淡蓝色宽袖长袍，银色细发簪。
<Subject 2> 是 <Picture 2> 中的年轻男子，束发，黑色长袍，深色皮革护腕。
<Subject 3> 是 <Picture 3> 中的女子，红色长袍，拖曳长飘带。
<Subject 4> 是 <Picture 4> 中的雪林场景，松枝覆雪，孤树红梅盛开，雪花飘落。

summary:
[reference generation] 目标视频跟随 <Subject 1> 与 <Subject 2> 两名同门，穿过 <Subject 4> 的暴风雪，直到看见 <Subject 3> 在红梅树下等候。三个镜头从侧向跟拍中景，切到远景揭示，最后落在 <Subject 1> 开口呼唤的特写。

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - 黑色长发、淡蓝宽袖长袍与银色发簪全程保留。
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - 束发、黑色长袍与深色皮革护腕全程保留。
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 2]): fully_preserved - 红色长袍与拖曳长飘带全程保留。
<Subject 4> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - 覆雪松林、盛开红梅与飘雪作为各镜头环境全程保留。

detailed_description:
目标视频为电影感武侠风格，冷蓝灰光线，大雪纷飞，浅景深。
[Shot 1] 中景侧向跟拍，<Subject 1> 与 <Subject 2> 在 <Subject 4> 齐膝深雪中前行，两侧覆雪松枝合拢，风卷雪花横穿画面。<Subject 1> 以宽袖挡风；<Subject 2> 落后半步。 <Subject 1> 骤然停步，眼中惊喜与如释重负，直视前方，镜头随其停住。
[Shot 2] At 00:02.000，切至沿视线方向的远景并缓慢推进。<Subject 4> 孤树红梅之下，<Subject 3> 背对镜头静立，红袍与长飘带是雪地中唯一的饱和色，飘带被风掀起。
[Shot 3] At 00:03.500，切至 <Subject 1> (S1) 正面特写，淡蓝长袍肩头积雪，眼眶含泪。<Subject 1> (S1) 以年轻女声、压抑而颤抖地开口，<d>[Chinese] 师姐，我们终于找到你了。</d> 她抿唇继续望向前方，风声渐起。

overall_soundscape:
全程呼啸风声与密集落雪，第一镜中有踩过深雪的闷响脚步声。

non_diegetic_music:
克制的二胡独奏慢板，低音弦乐持续铺垫，在最终特写处轻轻推高。

nodes.title: INSTRUCTIONS
widgets_values:
⚠️ **WARNING:** Always make a backup of your ComfyUI installation before updating or installing new custom nodes, so you can roll back if anything goes wrong.

## Prerequisites

- ComfyUI updated to the latest version (to access the new core nodes used in this workflow).

> **Node color legend**
> | Color | Meaning |
> |-------|---------|
> 🔴 Red | Instructional notes — read-only reference |
> 🟡 Yellow | Configurable elements — adjust to your needs |
> 🟣 Purple | Toggle switches — enable or disable option groups |

---

## General Instructions

**TIP:** Disable all groups at the start. This sets the workflow to a basic text-to-video mode. Then, enable groups one by one as needed.

Try not to manually bypass nodes. Instead, use the fast group bypasser switches; otherwise, you may accidentally bypass something important. As a general rule of thumb, if a group doesn't have a bypasser switch, it shouldn't be bypassed.

# 1. Reference Inputs

You can enable the reference inputs you need (audio, video, and images). With all reference inputs disabled, the workflow works as a standard text-to-video generator.

The title of each input indicates the reference tag you should use in your prompt (`<Audio N>`, `<Video N>`, `<Picture N>`).

Visit the [MiniMaxAI MiniMax-H3 official prompting guide](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md) for a better understanding of the prompt structure expected by the MiniMax model.

For videos, you can reference both the video and its audio content using the same video tag (`<Video N>`).

It is highly recommended that you enable the inputs in order. For example, try to avoid enabling Image 1, 3, and 5; instead, enable Image 1, 2, and 3.

For lip-sync and motion transfer, try to use reference media that is at least as long as your target video. Otherwise, the model will try to fill the gap, which may produce unexpected results.

Make sure only the desired reference inputs are enabled. Otherwise, unwanted reference content may leak into the generation.

# 2. Video Settings

- Set the video duration in the **"VIDEO DURATION (seconds)"** node.
- Set the video resolution in the **"Video resolution"** resolution master node. If you don't know how to use it, simply click on each dimension in the top-right corner of the node and enter your target resolution manually. You can also use the resolution table provided by the ComfyUI team to select a recommended resolution, but feel free to experiment. The workflow performs the necessary calculations to ensure that you always end up with safe video dimensions and lengths.
- Enable **"Half resolution"** and **"LTX2.3 Upscaler"** if you want to perform a two-pass run, similar to the workflow used by LTX. With this mode enabled, the first pass is generated at half the target resolution, and the result is then upscaled using the 2× LTX2.3 upscaler.

**TIP:** Use **Half res** first to perform a quick initial pass and check whether the result is good. Once you're satisfied with it, you can fix the seed and enable the other processing steps (LTX upscaler, NVIDIA upscaler, interpolation, etc.).

# 3. Prompt

You can use natural language to guide the generation. Just don't forget to mention your references using the proper tagging system (`<Audio N>`, `<Video N>`, `<Picture N>`).

Visit the [MiniMaxAI MiniMax-H3 official prompting guide](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md) for an in-depth prompting guide.

## Prompting Snippets (Quick Guide)

This is a quick guide, but it is not exhaustive. These basic prompt structures can help you quickly test the model, but they are not representative of its full capabilities.

You can mix and match the following examples to construct your final prompt.

### Character Identity Lock

`<Subject X>` is the young woman with short brown hair and bangs, wearing a pink studded leather jacket over a white shirt and blue jeans, whose appearance comes from `<Picture X>`.

### First, Middle, or Last Frames

This is a little hit-or-miss. The FL2VA model is better suited for this, but MiniMax-H3 is still capable of locking frames to specific segments of the video, including the first and last frames.

`<Picture X>` is the first frame of Shot X, depicting `<Subject X>` singing into the microphone in the recording studio.

You can also explicitly define the timing:

`[Shot X] At 00:00.000, the scene opens in <Picture X>...`

### Lip-Sync

`<Audio X>` is reused in full as the target video's audio track. `<Subject X>` performs with expressive body language and facial movements, perfectly lip-syncing to `<Audio X>`.

### Voice Cloning

`<Audio X>` is the voice-timbre reference for `<Subject X>` (SX).

`<Audio X>` (voice reference): the target speaker (SX) follows the timbre and tone of the original signal without copying it directly.

### Scenes / Video Segments

`[Shot X] At 00:00.000, ...`

`[Shot X] At 00:03.000, ...`

# 4. Extra Nodes

## LTX 2× Upscaler

- Upscales the output by 2×.

**Best use:**
- Combine with **Half resolution** mode for improved speed and quality.

**Optional:** By default, this upscaler uses the first frame of the generated video as its reference. However, you can select one of the reference images as the main upscaling reference (first frame) by selecting it in the **"Upscaler reference image"** group.

This works like the standard LTX upscaler used in LTX workflows, so make sure the selected image is the first frame, or very close to it.

**Use the Easy Global Seed node in the sampling section to set your seed.**

## NVIDIA VSR Upscaler

A fast upscaler using Video Super Resolution. Select a target resolution, and the workflow will perform the necessary calculations to match that target resolution. It is compatible with custom video sizes.

## Interpolation

Smooths the video by adding additional frames, increasing the frame rate according to the selected FPS multiplier.
